name: NewsletterMaker Lite
author: Mel Lewis (obitmaker999)

sections.description:
NewsletterMaker Lite lets you build beautifully laid-out newsletters directly inside WordPress, without touching a single line of code. Perfect for membership organisations, clubs, associations, and community groups that publish regular newsletters.

Build your newsletter with a visual editor:

  • Add sections with a choice of layouts — text only, image left, image right, image above and below
  • Choose image sizes to suit your content — small portrait shots for reports, medium for articles
  • Add headlines, body text, captions and image galleries
  • Auto-generated Table of Contents from your section headings
  • Reorder sections by dragging and dropping
  • Section templates for common report types — Chairman’s Report, Editor’s Report, and more

Preview and export:

  • Full-screen preview showing exactly how your newsletter will look
  • Print to PDF directly from the browser — no additional software required

Manage your newsletters:

  • Newsletter list with issue number, date and section count at a glance
  • Keep a skeleton newsletter as a reference for your regular standing sections

NewsletterMaker Pro adds powerful publishing features:

  • Generate print-quality PDFs server-side using the mPDF library
  • Publish newsletters as standalone web pages on your site — outside your theme, beautifully formatted
  • Copy Forward — create next month’s issue from this month’s in one click
  • Continuation sections — flow long articles across multiple sections with different image layouts
  • Featured image caption and Editor’s Note
  • Half-page and full-page advertisement layouts
  • Save PDF directly to your server archive folder
  • Published Issues admin screen — manage all your live newsletters

Upgrade to NewsletterMaker Pro
sections.installation:
1. Upload the newslettermaker-lite folder to /wp-content/plugins/
  2. Activate the plugin through the Plugins menu in WordPress
  3. Go to NewsletterMaker Lite → Settings and enter your organisation name, newsletter title and logo
  4. Go to NewsletterMaker Lite → Add New to create your first newsletter

Recommended first steps:

  • Set up your organisation details in Settings before creating your first newsletter
  • Build a skeleton newsletter with your regular standing sections and keep it as a reference
  • Use that reference when adding the standing sections to each new issue
sections.faq:
Does this work with any WordPress theme?

Yes — the newsletter editor works independently of your theme. The preview page is a standalone page outside your theme.

Can members read the newsletter online?

The Lite preview is available to authorised WordPress editors. Use browser print to create a PDF for members. NewsletterMaker Pro can publish a standalone web page with its own URL.

Can I generate a PDF?

The free version supports browser print to PDF from the authorised preview. NewsletterMaker Pro adds server-side PDF generation using the mPDF library.

Do I need any technical knowledge?

No coding required at all. If you can use WordPress, you can use NewsletterMaker Lite.

Can I use this for a printed newsletter?

Yes — use the Print button in the preview to print or save as PDF. For a professionally formatted PDF, upgrade to NewsletterMaker Pro.

How do I create next month’s newsletter?

In NewsletterMaker Pro, use the Copy Forward feature to create a new issue from the previous one with all your standing sections already in place. In the free version, create a new newsletter and add your sections manually.

Is there a limit on the number of newsletters or sections?

No limits — create as many newsletters and sections as you need.
